description:
## Why

`apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/components/assistant_message.ex:68` defines:

```elixir
defp normalize_md(text), do: text |> String.trim() |> String.replace("\t", "   ")
```

This is called on the **entire snapshot binary** every chunk inside `refresh_streams/2`. For a 10 KB streaming message, that's a fresh 10 KB binary allocation per chunk — independent of any agent-side fix and independent of `Markdown.Render`'s otherwise-incremental work.

`Markdown.Render` already does `String.replace(text, "\t", "   ")` inside `render_segment/2` on the volatile tail only. The right place for both transforms is inside `Markdown.Render` itself, applied to the volatile tail (size bounded by the current paragraph), not to the cumulative snapshot.

## Shape

Move the normalization into `Markdown.Render`:

- Tab → spaces happens already on the segment, on every render. Leaving it.
- Trim is the awkward bit — `String.trim/1` strips leading whitespace too, which is undesirable mid-stream. The actual need is "strip a leading newline that some providers emit." Replace `String.trim/1` at the call site with a one-shot leading-whitespace strip applied to `source` only when the renderer first sees non-empty content. Or: drop the trim entirely and let the lexer's blank-line semantics handle it.

Read the existing tests for AssistantMessage.update_content / `Markdown` rendering to confirm what trim is actually doing for callers, and whether removing it changes any byte-equality expectations.

## Acceptance

- `AssistantMessage.update_block/3` (post-`.9`) does no per-snapshot allocation proportional to total message size.
- `Markdown.Render`'s output is byte-equal to the prior pipeline for representative inputs (golden tests).
- `normalize_md` removed from `assistant_message.ex`.

## Tests

- Streaming-trim test: a message that begins with a leading newline still renders without that leading blank.
- Streaming with embedded tabs renders identically to before.
- Byte-equality: `Markdown.Render` output for several fixtures matches `Markdown.render` (already covered by `render_test.exs`; extend if any new normalization moves in).

## Out of scope

- Other `String.trim` / `String.replace` per-chunk patterns in `interactive.ex` (none currently identified, but flag if discovered).

## Notes

Discovered during deep-research review of `.6` / agent event redesign. Independent of those tickets — this is a TUI-side allocation issue.
title: Move trim/tab normalization into Markdown.Render
